claim.quote: Here we show that antihydrogen atoms, released from magnetic confinement in the ALPHA-g apparatus, behave in a way consistent with gravitational attraction to the Earth.

date.note: Nature publication date; no earlier preprint date was found in a fetched source.

key_value_text.quote: Repulsive ‘antigravity’ is ruled out in this case.
key_value_text.value: Antihydrogen released from the trap behaves consistently with gravitational attraction; antigravity ruled out in this case

name: Observation of the effect of gravity on the motion of antimatter

significance.quote: Repulsive ‘antigravity’ is ruled out in this case.
significance.value: Consistent with gravitational attraction; repulsive antigravity ruled out (no sigma level stated in the abstract)

summary.plain: ALPHA-g released antihydrogen atoms from a magnetic trap and saw them behave in a way consistent with gravitational attraction to Earth. The abstract states that repulsive antigravity is ruled out in this case.
summary.technical: Antihydrogen released from magnetic confinement in the vertical ALPHA-g apparatus behaves consistently with gravitational attraction to the Earth; repulsive antigravity is ruled out. The abstract describes it as paving the way for precision tests of the weak equivalence principle for antimatter.

title: Observation of the effect of gravity on the motion of antimatter
why_it_matters: The abstract says the experiment paves the way for precision studies of the gravitational acceleration between anti-atoms and the Earth to test the weak equivalence principle.
